# Fresh-instance test of exact term-request filtering

Development used the fourteen odd-numbered CSPLib instances. On the even-numbered instances, test the simpler interval filter selected after seeing the development results. The mechanism is established constraint propagation. The research question concerns additional exact-search cost on the load-optimal curriculum service. Hold out even-numbered instances until the solver, sampler, endpoints and comparison set are recorded. The generated requests and mathematical feasibility are independent of teacher judgments.

For every even instance certify the smallest peak using the same deterministic budget and search procedure as development. Sample sixteen pairs of placements over all periods and sixteen over individual precedence windows, with the instance number as seed and no duplicated pair of placements. Return an actual feasible timetable or an infeasibility decision. Keep all unresolved cases. A scenario is independent of every previous scenario; the shared base model may be reused. Exclude base peak certification and common loading from service timings, include precomputation specific to a method.

Compare a reused CP-SAT template with five policies: integer search alone; precedence precheck; preceding check plus singleton capacity; preceding bounds plus all contiguous capacities; and interval precheck plus cumulative assignment LP. In addition, compare the interval method against a CP solver that directly narrows periods to propagated bounds for cases passing precedence (no separate capacity tests). Give search one worker and three deterministic units. Every method must return a validated witness or the same certified infeasibility as the reference. Unknown or inconsistent cases prevent calling the service equivalent on the full evaluation set. Count CP calls. Wall times include query handling, clone, any prechecks, solve and witness materialization, and exclude offline verification. Use three shuffled orders for every benchmark/request on a fixed CPU. Summarize median time per method/request, average within each benchmark, and use the geometric mean of benchmark-level ratios. Report per-instance ratios and paired bootstrap intervals over the fourteen instances (fixed seed 6723, 10,000 resamples, Bonferroni limits for five comparisons). A strong speed win requires 10% lower time against each comparator and simultaneous positive improvement. Mathematical feasibility parity is a distinct endpoint. Runtime has no equivalence margin. The benchmark family shares a generator and is one external source.
